what: Scrapbook board pieces attach one by one at times (ms) set for each — names are cut in from below and rise (.81s), photos and notes drop from the upper right at −2.6° and settle after overshooting 0.8° (.47s), stamps and stickers are pressed in from .84× (.38s bouncy curve), text either rises (.45s) or is written slantwise like handwriting (.34s), and underlines are drawn from the left (.38s)
ease: Default cubic-bezier(0.2,0.72,0.22,1) · drop cubic-bezier(0.24,0.68,0.26,1) · press cubic-bezier(0.3,1.5,0.5,1)

options.on: load (default — as soon as it is attached) · scroll (when the panel reaches 80% of the screen)
options.rate: Time multiplier, default 1 — multiplies the piece’s --seq(ms). The original already has tempo × .7 written in

use:
Your name here

Stamp

from.where: index.html hero collage (.h-stage .h-piece[data-place] — --seq from the original BEAT×0.7 order table)

note: data-key is the attach type: name·drop·press·rise·write·rule, and without it the piece rises slightly as it appears. Timing per piece is --seq (ms) in style. The original locks scrolling until assembly ends, but the part doesn’t lock (only in site code index.js). With reduced motion, shows the fully attached look right away
